title: Resource groups and subscriptions: lifecycle, moves, quotas and directories
learningObjective: Create, organise, move and delete resources across resource groups and subscriptions safely. Manage subscription settings: resource providers, quotas, directory and billing owner.
foundation: A resource group is a container for related resources that share a lifecycle, such as everything for one application. Delete the group and everything inside it is deleted.
Every resource belongs to exactly one resource group, and resource groups cannot be nested. Resources in one group can live in different regions.
A subscription is the billing and management boundary above resource groups. It trusts one Microsoft Entra tenant for sign-in and has its own limits (quotas).
You can move resources to another resource group or subscription. They keep running and stay in the same region, but their resource IDs change.
engineer: Resource group location: it only says where the group's own details (metadata) are stored. If that region goes down, you can't update the group, but resources in other regions keep running.
No renaming: you can't rename a resource group. Create a new one and move the resources into it.

Before you move resources: validate first (the portal does this for you); move things that depend on each other together, such as a VM with its disks and network card (NIC); check the move-support table, because some types can't move (for example AKS clusters).

During and after a move: both resource groups are locked for changes while the move runs. Roles given directly on a moved resource don't move with it. Resource IDs change. The region stays the same; moving to another region is a different job (Azure Resource Mover or redeploying).
Moving to another subscription: both subscriptions must be in the same Entra tenant, and the target must have the needed resource providers registered.
Deleting a resource group: everything inside is deleted, in the right order. A lock on anything inside stops the delete. az group delete --no-wait returns at once, but the delete can take minutes.

Subscription jobs: register resource providers (such as Microsoft.ContainerInstance or Microsoft.Insights) before you use a service; check and raise quotas (for example vCPUs per VM family per region) under Usage + quotas; rename the subscription; add tags, budgets, policies and roles (RBAC) at subscription level.
Moving a subscription to another Entra tenant (change directory): all its Azure role assignments are deleted for good, managed identities break, and Key Vaults need their tenant updated.
Changing who pays (billing ownership transfer): a separate job. It doesn't change the directory.
Cancelling a subscription: billing stops and the subscription is disabled, so resources can't be reached. You can reactivate it for up to 90 days, then it and its data are deleted.

example.title: Splitting a shared resource group
body: rg-shared holds a web app and a shared storage account. They have different owners and different lifecycles. The team creates rg-web and moves the App Service plan and web app together, because they depend on each other. Then they give roles on the new resource group.
Two roles had been given directly on the web app. They didn't move, so the team creates them again. Scripts that used the old resource ID are updated.

prerequisites: Write access on both the source and target resource groups
For moves between subscriptions: same tenant, and providers registered in the target
permissions: Owner on the subscription, to change its directory
limits: Resource groups can't be renamed or put inside each other
Resources keep their region when moved
Quotas are per subscription (and often per region)
portal: Resource groups > Create: subscription, name, region (metadata location), tags.
Resource group > select resources > Move > to another resource group / subscription / region (region launches Resource Mover). Review validation, then confirm that IDs will change.
Resource group > Delete resource group: type the name to confirm.
Subscriptions > choose one > Resource providers (register), Usage + quotas (request an increase), Overview > Rename / Change directory / Cancel subscription.
configuration.cli:
az group create --name rg-app-prod --location westeurope --tags costCenter=CC-100
ids=$(az resource list -g rg-app --query "[?contains(name,'vm-web')].id" -o tsv)
az resource move --destination-group rg-app-prod --ids $ids
az resource move --destination-group rg-app --destination-subscription-id <target-sub-id> --ids <storage-account-id>
az group delete --name rg-old --yes --no-wait
az account set --subscription sub-app1
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ContainerInstance
az vm list-usage --location westeurope -o table
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-app-prod -Location westeurope -Tag @{ costCenter = 'CC-100' }
$ids = (Get-AzResource -ResourceGroupName rg-app | Where-Object Name -like 'vm-web*').ResourceId
Move-AzResource -DestinationResourceGroupName rg-app-prod -ResourceId $ids
Remove-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-old -Force
Set-AzContext -Subscription 'sub-app1'
Register-AzResourceProvider -ProviderNamespace Microsoft.ContainerInstance
Get-AzVMUsage -Location westeurope

lab.objective: Plan resource moves that pass validation, and explain the side effects of moves and directory changes.
steps: Open the Move resources tab. Move only vm-web and read why validation fails.
Add its disk and NIC and move again. Note the changed IDs and the role assignment warning.
Open Subscription directory and simulate a directory change.
expected: A VM without its dependents fails validation
Direct role assignments are reported as not moved

troubleshooting.symptom: Move validation fails with 'resources not in the same resource group' or missing-dependency errors.
troubleshooting.cause: Something the resource depends on wasn't included, or the resources come from several groups.
troubleshooting.fix: Include everything it depends on, and move from one source group at a time.

troubleshooting.cause: The resource provider isn't registered in the subscription.

troubleshooting.symptom: A deployment fails with a QuotaExceeded or OperationNotAllowed vCPU error.
troubleshooting.cause: You've used all your vCPU quota for that VM family in that region.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask for more in Usage + quotas, or pick another size or region.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users lost access after the subscription moved to another tenant.
troubleshooting.cause: Changing the directory deletes all role assignments.
troubleshooting.fix: Give roles again to people in the new tenant.

troubleshooting.cause: Something inside is locked, or a resource in another group depends on something inside.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the lock or the dependency first.

comparisons.difference: Management groups hold subscriptions, for rules and access. Resource groups hold resources inside one subscription.

comparisons.service: AWS accounts and tags / resource groups
comparisons.difference: An AWS account is like an Azure subscription. AWS Resource Groups are just saved tag searches; they don't own resources.

misconceptions.myth: Resources must be in the same region as their resource group.
misconceptions.reality: No. The group's location only stores its details. Resources can be in any region.

misconceptions.myth: Moving a resource to another resource group moves it to another region.
misconceptions.reality: No. The region stays the same. The resource ID changes.

misconceptions.myth: You can rename a resource group.
misconceptions.reality: No. Create a new one and move the resources.

misconceptions.myth: Moving a subscription to another directory keeps its roles.
misconceptions.reality: No. All role assignments are deleted.

architectureDecisions: Group by lifecycle and owner: put things that are created, changed and deleted together in one resource group, not all VMs in one and all storage in another.
Use subscriptions for strong separation: separate bills, separate quotas, and a problem in one doesn't spread. Use resource groups for each application.
Give roles on the resource group: not on single resources, so moves and redeployments don't leave roles behind.

steps.label: Messy
steps.title: Hundreds of resources, no structure
body: Without structure you cannot delete a whole project, give one team access, or see what one app costs.

steps.label: Resource groups
steps.title: A resource group is a folder with rules
body: Every resource lives in exactly one resource group. Put things with the same lifecycle together, so you can manage access, tags, locks and deletion as one unit.
The group has a region (for its metadata), but the resources inside can be in any region.

callout.text: Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it.

steps.label: Move
steps.title: Moving resources
body: You can move most resources to another resource group or subscription. The resource keeps its region; the move only changes its resource ID. Azure validates the move first, and both groups are locked for writes during it.
Some resources cannot move, or must move together with related ones (for example a VM with its disks and NIC).

callout.text: Moving to another region is different: use Azure Resource Mover or redeploy.

steps.label: Subscriptions
steps.title: Subscriptions: billing, access and limits
body: A subscription is a billing unit and a boundary for access and limits. It trusts exactly one Microsoft Entra tenant. Moving a subscription to another tenant removes all its role assignments.

Quotas limit things like vCPUs per region. View them in Usage + quotas and request an increase if needed. Resource providers (such as Microsoft.Compute) must be registered before you use a service, which usually happens automatically.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Resource groups and subscriptions
body: Group by lifecycle; know your limits.
recap: Resources can be in other regions than their group
Moves keep the region and change the ID
Subscriptions trust one tenant; moving tenants drops role assignments
Check Usage + quotas before big deployments

handsOn.title: Move a storage account between resource groups and read your quotas
handsOn.cost: Free, apart from cents for an empty storage account.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Create a second resource group: rg-az104-lab-2 in the same region.
Create a storage account in rg-az104-lab (Standard, LRS).
Open the storage account > Overview > Move (next to 'Resource group') > Move to another resource group. Choose rg-az104-lab-2.
steps.see: Azure validates the move first. Wait for 'Validation succeeded'.

steps.do: Tick the box that says tools and scripts must be updated, then Move.
steps.see: After a minute the storage account appears in rg-az104-lab-2. Its resource ID now contains rg-az104-lab-2.

steps.do: Search 'Subscriptions' > your subscription > Settings > Usage + quotas. Filter Provider: Compute and region: your region.
steps.see: Your 'Total Regional vCPUs' limit and current usage.

steps.do: In the same subscription open Settings > Resource providers and search for Microsoft.Compute.
Open the subscription Overview and note the Directory (tenant) it belongs to.
steps.see: Your subscription ID and parent tenant.

check: The storage account moved and kept its region.
You found your regional vCPU quota.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
